recent_articles.title: Latvian PM resigns due to split in alliance over Russian drones
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Evika Silina**, the Latvian prime minister, resigned after disagreements over drone incidents from Ukraine led to the collapse of her coalition government. **Edgars Rinkevics**, the president, will hold consultations with political parties on Friday as they attempt to form a new government. The Progressive Party withdrew its support for Silina following her dismissal of defense minister **Andris Spruds**.  The opposition United List is prepared to manage the new administration and has called for a motion of no confidence against Silina.

recent_articles.title: India no longer a country that suffers, will strike back if Pakistan provokes us again: Rajnath Singh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Defence Minister Rajnath Singh** warned **Pakistan** against terrorism, stating that India would respond decisively if provoked again.  He highlighted the "Operation Sindoor" campaign as a strong message to Pakistan and emphasized India's zero-tolerance policy towards terrorism, citing past military actions like the 2016 surgical strikes and 2019 Balakot airstrikes. **Singh** also condemned the Pahalgam terror attack last year, stating that India would not tolerate attacks on its citizens.

recent_articles.title: Security stepped up for visit of Chandrababu Naidu, Rajnath Singh to Puttaparthi on May 15 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu** and **Union Minister for Defence Rajnath Singh** are scheduled to visit Puttaparthi on May 15th to lay the foundation stone for a ₹1 lakh crore fifth-generation fighter aircraft manufacturing project.  The project will span 650 acres and is expected to create significant employment opportunities in the region.  **District Collector A. Shyam Prasad** oversaw security arrangements, including electricity, medical, and fire services on standby at the venue. **Superintendent of Police S. Satish Kumar** reviewed security measures for both the event and **Lokesh’s** visit to Battalapalli on May 14th.

recent_articles.title: Assam swearing-in LIVE: Himanta Biswa Sarma takes oath as Assam CM; Four MLAs sworn in as Ministers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma** was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Assam for a second consecutive term on Tuesday, May 2, 2026. **Governor Lakshman Prasad Acharya** administered the oath of office at a ceremony held at the Veterinary Ground in Guwahati.  Joining **Sarma** were four other MLAs who took oaths as Ministers: **Rameswar Teli**, **Ajanta Neog**, **Atul Bora**, and **Charan Boro**. The event was attended by prominent figures including **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, Nitin Gadkari, Sarbananda Sonowal, Pabitra Margherita**, and **BJP president Nitin Nabin**. This marks the formation of a third successive NDA government in the state.

recent_articles.title: NDA leaders stake claim to form Assam government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, leader of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**-led **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)**, was unanimously elected as the leader of the Assam Legislature Party.  Following this, the NDA staked a claim to form the government in Assam with the support of 102 MLAs. The swearing-in ceremony for the new council of ministers is scheduled for May 12th. **J.P. Nadda**, Union Minister and central observer for the BJP Legislature Party meeting, announced that eight BJP legislators proposed Sarma's name as their leader.  The newly elected members of the BJP and its regional allies — **Asom Gana Parishad (AGP)** and **Bodoland People’s Front (BPF)** — chose their leaders in the morning.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet 2026: From Dilip Ghosh to Agnimitra Paul, Ministers who were sworn in along with Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, newly sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, inducted five new ministers into his cabinet on Saturday. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, J. P. Nadda, and Dharmendra Pradhan**, among other BJP leaders.  **Dilip Ghosh**, a senior BJP leader who secured victory in the Kharagpur seat, **Agnimitra Paul**, a fashion designer-turned-legislator who won Asansol Dakshin, **Ashok Kirtania**, a BJP stalwart who gained victory in Bangaon Uttar, and **Kshudiram Tudu**, a former school teacher from Ranibandh (ST) constituency, were among the newly appointed ministers.  **Nisith Pramanik**, a key face of BJP from North Bengal, was also inducted into the cabinet.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal: Modi's BJP conquers one of India's toughest political frontiers
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won a decisive victory in West Bengal, marking a significant breakthrough for **Narendra Modi** and his 12-year reign.  This unexpected outcome comes after years of the party's struggle to gain traction in the state, which has traditionally been dominated by the Trinamool Congress (TMC). The BJP's success is attributed to a combination of factors, including its aggressive welfare pitch, sharpened Hindu consolidation efforts, and a focus on alleged corruption within the TMC. This victory will likely have far-reaching implications for the BJP's future trajectory, potentially solidifying **Amit Shah**'s position as Modi's successor.

recent_articles.title: India halted Sindoor on its own terms: Rajnath - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rajnath Singh**, India's Defence Minister, sharply criticized **Pakistan** at the National Security Summit 2.0 for its support of terrorism and its role as a global hub for it. He defended India's decision to halt Operation Sindoor voluntarily, emphasizing that India was prepared for a prolonged conflict if necessary.  Singh asserted that India's approach sends a clear message that there will be no distinction between terrorists and their sponsors.

recent_articles.title: Italy told to avoid sharing of defence tech with Pakistan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rajnath Singh**, India's Defence Minister, met with his Italian counterpart, **Guido Crosetto**, to discuss a range of issues including regional and global security concerns.  Singh urged Italy to refrain from sharing sensitive defence technologies with Pakistan, emphasizing India's security interests. The two leaders reaffirmed the strong partnership between India and Italy, highlighting avenues for further cooperation in defense industrial development and information sharing. A Bilateral Military Cooperation Plan was exchanged outlining future engagements between the armed forces of both countries.

recent_articles.title: Congress accuses Rajnath Singh of giving 'clean chit to Pakistan', dubs his remarks at SCO 'anti-national' - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh accused **Defence Minister Rajnath Singh** of giving a "shameful clean chit" to **Pakistan** at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in Bishkek. Ramesh claimed this new stance is part of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's policy of appeasement towards the U.S. and China, citing Singh's statement that "terrorism has no nationality or theology."  Ramesh also questioned whether Pakistan harbors terrorist camps targeting India.

recent_articles.title: Mali violence escalates: Defence minister Sadio Camara killed in 'terrorist attack' - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The security crisis in Mali escalated significantly after the death of defense minister Sadio Camara, who was killed in an attack on his residence.  **Al-Qaeda-linked militants**, **Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM)**, and the **Tuareg-led separatist group Azawad Liberation Front (FLA)** coordinated attacks targeting Bamako and other cities, leaving at least 16 people injured. **United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres** condemned the violence, while **ECOWAS** called for stronger regional cooperation to counter rising militant violence in the Sahel.  The attacks signal a worrying shift in the security situation, potentially complicating counterinsurgency efforts in Mali and neighboring countries.
